Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Recent work separates persistent preferences, transient intent, and multiple concurrent interests. [Ma et al. (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.knosys.2024.112657) combine interest subgraphs, temporal analysis, and contrastive separation of interests. [IBLSRec (2025)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10820829/) distinguishes stable item relationships from short-lived associations and uses latent intent to refine preferences. [DSRec (September 2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21548) explicitly separates historical aggregation from local, time-gap-modulated intent using two state-space branches; relevant architectural inspiration, but its abstract does not establish computational savings against this SASRec benchmark.

Repeated intent need not mean repurchasing the identical item. [HyperHawkes (WWW 2025)](https://evazangerle.at/publication/peintner-www-2025/) learns latent intents through hypergraphs and contrastive clustering, models recurrence with Hawkes processes, and combines these signals with short-term attention. Complementarity also differs from co-occurrence: [2025 consumer research](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jretai.2025.01.006) studies distinct effects of usage complementarity and basket association; it does not validate inferring functional complements from sequential logs alone.

Lightweight adaptation hypothesis: retain SASRec, add a pooled long-term history branch and a few learned interest queries, then gate their scores against recent-context scores using time gaps and history support. Ablate pooling, multiple interests, and temporal gating separately under the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Treat reduced overreaction to isolated purchases, recurring needs, and complementary transitions as hypotheses requiring validation. Interaction histories cannot establish satisfaction or completed needs; unseen-item evaluation makes intent recurrence more applicable than direct repeat-item boosting. Published gains do not establish gains under this benchmark.

---

Recent work supports combining sequential prediction with item graphs, while separating similarity from complementarity. [SComGNN (AAAI 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02130) models complementary products as relevant yet functionally dissimilar, combining low-pass and mid-pass graph filters. [SAGERec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/24/4844) combines a global semantic graph with a lightweight Transformer, but uses LLM-derived representations, incompatible with the no-pretrained-weights constraint. [STAR (CIKM 2024)](https://pure.uva.nl/ws/files/245900224/3627673.3679999.pdf) demonstrates interpretable sparse term matching, but its BERT-based architecture and user-review inputs also prevent direct adoption here.

A constraint-compatible research hypothesis: retain SASRec; add a small, directed graph of transitions observed exclusively in training histories and a separate title/description similarity branch. Encode text using local TF–IDF word/character features with a learned projection, or randomly initialized token embeddings pooled and trained jointly with next-item prediction. Keep graph neighborhoods sparse and learn a residual gate so content associations cannot dominate sequence evidence. These are proposed adaptations, not published performance guarantees; compare sequence-only, graph-only additions, text-only additions and their combination using macro validation HR@10.

Treat transition edges as behavioral associations and lexical similarity as content overlap: neither establishes substitutes, complements or physical compatibility. Reserve explicit compatibility claims for available descriptions that name a supported model, connector or standard; generic shared terminology remains uncertain. Preserve separate evidence channels and retain original model identifiers during tokenization. Learn all representations from permitted data, without review text, relation labels from external datasets or pretrained weights.

---

Stronger multi-negative training is a credible SASRec improvement. [gSASRec’s IJCAI 2024 summary](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) combines multiple negatives with generalized BCE to reduce sampling-induced overconfidence; recommended settings are 128–256 negatives and calibration parameter t=0.75. [eSASRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06450) identifies sampled softmax plus improved Transformer layers as a strong combination without extra item features, although its results do not isolate the loss’s contribution. These findings support testing multi-negative sampled softmax and gBCE before adding complex auxiliary contrastive objectives.

Hardness needs moderation. [R²NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) reports early instability and false-negative risks from aggressive mining; it uses warm-start training, progressively adjusted difficulty, and stochastic selection among top-ranked candidates. Its experiments show deterministic hard-negative sampling can underperform uniform sampling. A practical adaptation: retain uniform negatives, introduce a modest mined fraction after warm-up, sample among several high-scoring candidates, and exclude observed training-history items and the current positive. This reduces known-positive collisions but cannot identify every latent positive.

For Electronics, these are hypotheses requiring validation. A [2024 sampling comparison](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds dataset-dependent trade-offs: popularity-based and in-batch negatives can balance popularity bands while lowering aggregate accuracy. Suggested ablation: existing BCE versus multi-negative sampled softmax versus gBCE, then add warmed-up stochastic mining to the best objective. ## Starting Research Idea
SASRec predicts the next interaction using causal self-attention over a user's item history. Learned item and position embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting features score candidate items by dot product. Attention can emphasize recent interactions or draw on longer histories. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781).
